claims.text: The target material consists of W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix.
A W/Cu powder mixture can be mechanically activated before spark-plasma sintering using short-duration planetary milling.
Mechanical activation cleans oxide films from powder-particle surfaces.
Mechanical activation crushes or roughens particles and increases the contact area between components.
Oxide removal and increased contact area enhance interfacial bonding between W and Cu.
Mechanical activation facilitates diffusion and W–Cu interfacial bonding during lower-temperature SPS consolidation.
Mechanical activation before SPS reduces void formation in W–Cu composites.
Mechanical activation before SPS reduces phase separation in W–Cu composites.
The activated material will have a more uniform microstructure and near-perfect W–Cu contact than material made by conventional SPS of non-activated powders.
Mechanical activation will significantly improve thermal conductivity relative to conventional SPS of non-activated W/Cu powders.
Mechanical activation will improve mechanical strength and durability relative to conventional SPS of non-activated W/Cu powders.
Conventional SPS of non-activated W/Cu powders often produces phase separation and voids that compromise thermal transport and durability.
Processing will be conducted under inert atmosphere at temperatures far below the W melting point and Cu boiling point.
The consolidated material is intended for irradiation exposure typical of fusion-reactor joints.
The intervention is expected to work only when oxide contamination is moderate and activation time is optimized.
Extreme irradiation or variation in starting-powder quality may require additional process modifications.
